newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Firm Capers lead stronger market.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Firm Capers lead stronger market.

text.p: The freight market has started the week in uneventful fashion but brokers reported the firmer trend for Capers continuing worldwide while Panamaxes were unchanged.
Conditions were weak for Handies in the Atlantic on Monday but slightly stronger for these types in the east, shipbrokers said. The Baltic Freight Index rose four points to 1,511.
GRAIN
Little grain activity was noted for Panamaxes but Continental booked Panagiotis A 71,550 dwt delivery USGulf Jan 20 trip China at an easier $15,500 daily plus $350,000 bonus.
Mitsubishi were reported to have fixed the Halla-relet Sea Diamond for 52-54,000 tonnes heavy grain USGulf/Japan for Jan 20/25 at a firmer $26.85 no combo, in contrast to Friday's report of $27.25.
Cargill remained open for Handy upto Caper-size for Mississippi/Continent for Jan/Feb and for upto 85,000 tonnes heavy grain Mississippi/Egypt for early Feb.
Ice problems in the upper Mississippi were said to be impeding the flow of grain to the elevators which some believed could cause delays to tonnage loading down-river.
Meanwhile handy-size grain rates in the Atlantic have remained soft, partly influenced by the presence of lakers now seeking employment until the St Lawrence seaway reopens.

Fixing from the Plate included Beta 1,685,000 cft grain Up River and Necochea/Seaforth (max 50,000 disbursements) for Jan 16/22 at a lumpsum of $715,000. Andre were on subjects for 15,000 wheat and 5,000 soyabean meals Up River/Labuan and Kuching for Jan 20/30 and Continental with Evmar for 25,000 tonnes Plate/Tunisia possibly at $21.00, but full details were lacking.

Fresh orders were quoted by Soufflet 50,000 heavy grain Bahia Blanca/Red Sea for Jan 29/Feb 5, Cargill 700,000/800,000 cft Brazil/Continent prompt, Glencore 25,000 meals Mississippi/Spanish Med prompt, and Toepfer 900,000/1,200,000 cft Paranagua/Gibraltar-Hamburg for Jan 18/25 and 25,000 wheat Nantes-Montoir range/Umm Qas for Jan 18/25.

In the east Pan Ocean were linked with Ocean Pearl 61,800 dwt NoPac/South Korea, Captain John L 64,000 dwt was rumoured fixed delivery Far East via Australia to the Med, possibly via Egypt, at $7,100 daily, and Maywal fixed Saqqara 41,543 dwt delivery south Australia for grain to Yemen at $8,100 daily plus $180,000 bonus.
MINERALS

Owners' brokers were optimistic about prospects for Capers in all areas. There were rumours of 200,000 tonnes ironore Tubarao/Japan fixed at between $10.00 and $11.00 for Feb 15/28, and 110,000 coal Hampton Roads/Rotterdam at $6.50.

Chinese charterers covered 130,000/10 ironore Saldanha Bay/Beilun for mid Feb on subjects at $8.00, and Comanche 162,800 dwt was rumoured fixed by Kleimar Hampton Roads to Dunkirk east for mid Feb on private terms.

Orient Trust 117,961 was believed fixed from Taiwan to the Continent with coal, but full details were lacking. BHP were said to have booked Merchant Paramount on subjects for 150,000 tonnes coal Hay Pointaranto for Feb 15/28 at $10.40.
Irongate 179,000 dwt was said to have been fixed with ironore from Brazil to the Continent.

The newbuilding Channel Navigator 170,000 dwt was fixed prompt ex yard Japan by Docenave for two laden legs via Roberts Bank and Brazil redelivery Atlantic at $15,500 daily for the first 50 days and $16,000 daily for the balance.

Docenave were also linked with Northern Light 65,592 dwt delivery U.S. east coast end Jan for 2-4 months, but details were lacking. Flag Rolaco was on subjects for 50,000/5 fertilizers Yuzhnny/China with Ameropa at $25.15.
HANDY-SIZE
Handies small handy-size rates were a little easier on the Continent, shipbrokers said.

Ld-seals fixed the economical Olympic Merit 29,611 dwt delivery Antwerp prompt trip Far East at $9,250 daily and Von Appen booked a Chinese-controlled 31,000 dwt craned bulker delivery Skaw trip via Baltic to the Far East at $9,500 daily.
Elsewhere IVS took Ethnos 29,000 dwt South Africa/Continent at $5,000 daily. Brokers reported more enquiry in the Far East for geared tonnage. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
